# Fixture Corpus

Reference for the synthetic test fixtures in this directory (the "fixture blueprint" the testing-harness spec refers to). The designs were informed by a private corpus of real student proposals (11 documents, mixed quality); nothing here maps to an identifiable original: topics are altered, all names and institutions removed, defect patterns generalized. Each proposal-fixture directory holds one proposal file plus an `expected.json` oracle calibrated against the check script; `g`-prefix web fixtures hold served web assets instead and carry no oracle, and `s`-prefix raw submissions (a student's email or export before any normalization — not a proposal, so not check-able) carry none either, nor do `p`-prefix papers (published work a student brings as a starting point).

## Corpus-derived failure taxonomy (aggregate, anonymized)

| Pattern | Frequency | Tested by |
|---|---|---|
| No research questions at all | ~4/11 | Check (RQ section empty), Write/Ideate (must elicit) |
| RQs phrased as implementation goals ("how can X be built") | dominant where RQs exist | L2 rubric, Review |
| Bibliography present but never cited in-text | ~6/11 | Check (defined-but-uncited warning) |
| < 3 scientific references / URL-only bibliographies | ~4/11 | Check ([references] min_count), lit-search |
| Mixed methodologies in one proposal | ~4/11 | Review rubric (single-method rule) |
| Forbidden content: work plans/Gantt, chapter outlines, expected results | very common | Check (forbidden headings, timeline size guard) |
| Personal data: matriculation numbers, addresses, supervisor names/emails | common | Check (warning regexes), Import (strip on import) |
| Passive voice pervasive (esp. German), first-person narrative slips | near-universal (de) | Check warnings, Review hint |
| Confidentiality markers ("confidential", "vertraulich", NDA remarks) in industry-context proposals | recurring in corporate topics | Check warning (theses get published) |
| Free-form section structures (Goal/Work-steps, Scope/Approach, …) | majority | Check (canonical sections), Import (restructure) |
| Vendor/commercial sources grounding core claims | recurring | Review rubric, lit-search venue preference |
| Figures | nearly absent (0–1 per proposal) | confirms D3 (img/ optional) |
| PDF production variety: Word, LaTeX, LLM-assisted (formatting artifacts, swallowed headings, missing title blocks) | across corpus | Import robustness |

## Planned fixtures

Each fixture = one proposal file in the new single-file format (plus, for Import tests, a rendered PDF variant). `seeded defects` split into **mechanical** (Check must flag deterministically) and **semantic** (L2 rubric / Review must catch). Topics are synthetic.

| id | lang | level | tier | shape | seeded defects |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `f01-narrative-sketch` | de | BSc | low | free-form "Goal / Work steps" narrative | mech: no RQ section, no in-text citations, forbidden work-plan heading; sem: first-person storytelling, no gap argument, unfalsifiable outcome |
| `f02-tool-comparison` | de | BSc | mid | Motivation/Objective/Work-steps + Gantt | mech: Gantt table under a legitimate `Zeitplan` heading (size guard, not forbidden heading), 2 URL-only refs (< min), no RQs; sem: evaluative goal never sharpened into questions |
| `f03-compliance-audit` | en | BSc | mid-high | numbered free-form incl. chapter outline + timetable, personal data on cover | mech: forbidden chapter-structure + timetable headings, matriculation/address patterns, work-package pseudo-RQs; sem: RQs are work packages, typos |
| `f04-dsr-vendor-heavy` | de | MSc | mid | TOC/abbreviations, 1 main + 4 sub-RQs, chapter outline | mech: forbidden outline, supervisor + matriculation on title page, duplicate reference entry, "vertraulich" title-page stamp; sem: vendor pages ground definitional claims, RQ sub-questions design-phrased |
| `f05-slr-interviews` | en | MSc | high | canonical 4 sections | mech: clean (control fixture); sem: mixed methodology (SLR + interviews) violating single-method rule, missing interview-ethics note |
| `f06-prototype-testbed` | en | BSc | mid-high | canonical 4 sections | mech: forward-dated reference year; sem: passive-heavy evaluation, 4-campaign scope risk without fallback, no architecture figure despite hardware topic |
| `f07-network-pathfinding` | en | BSc | mid | custom Scope/Requirements/RQ/Approach/Schedule | mech: forbidden schedule, supervisor named, 2 refs; sem: 3 of 4 RQs implementation-goal, one leading RQ, mid-document first-person switch, typos |
| `f08-concept-sketch` | de | BSc | low | Abstract/Intro/Objective/Solution/Work-steps | mech: no RQs, no real bibliography (prose URL list), no in-text markers, implementation-opener title (`Konzept für …`); sem: severe passive, goals as construction aims, unfalsifiable "concept" outcome |
| `f09-llm-compliance-docs` | en | MSc | high | near-canonical, work-plan table | mech: forbidden work-plan heading, no leading `# ` title line, refs never cited in-text, swallowed-heading formatting artifact (Import robustness); sem: 3 "which…" RQs lacking degree phrasing, mixed method |
| `f10-risk-scoring` | en | MSc | mid | free-form with supervisor block | mech: supervisor names + emails, undated phase table, refs never cited in-text, "confidential — internal use only" footer marker; sem: 2 of 4 RQs implementation-goal, none operationalized, evaluation leans on internal feedback |
| `f11-migration-architecture` | de | BSc | high | canonical + extra Scope/Summary sections | mech: extra non-canonical sections (warning), vendor-doc references; sem: RQ2 is yes/no, requirements read as spec list — near-target quality, tests that Review stays quiet on structure |

## Beyond-corpus fixtures (invented — no workspace source)

The corpus leaves real coverage holes; these fixtures are designed from the rules alone:

| id | lang | level | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `f00-clean-en` | en | MSc | Fully compliant control, converted from the legacy Jane Doe `proposal.tex` (migration step 3) — the only workspace-sourced entry here, listed for completeness. |
| `f12-clean-de` | de | BSc | Fully compliant **German** control — the corpus contains no compliant German proposal at all. Tests canonical de section titles, de citation locale, Review staying silent. |
| `f13-pure-slr` | en | MSc | Pure Systematic Literature Review with its required subsections (search strategy / quality assessment and extracted information / synthesis) — corpus only has SLR *mixed* with interviews (f05). Exercises that branch of the methodology→subsection table. |
| `f14-user-study` | de | BSc | Pure User Study (preparation / procedure / analysis) — methodology entirely absent from the corpus. |
| `f17-theoretical` | en | BSc | Pure Theoretical Analysis (formalization / requirements / example) — corpus theoretical proposals (f03, f08) are free-form and defect-laden; the compliant branch is untested without this. |
| `f15-format-broken` | en | BSc | Trailing-YAML guardrail fixture: missing blank line before `---`, boolean-literal citation key (`on`), duplicate metadata block, leftover `[TODO: …]`, exactly 2 references ([references] min_count boundary), a three-word `# ` title (below the English `min_words` bound), and the only fixture keeping an `author:` key — it owns the anonymity tripwire. Tiny file, pure Check-mechanics oracle. |
| `f16-figures-import` | en | MSc | Invented PDF containing two figures — the corpus is nearly figure-free, so Import's `img/`-TODO path has no ground truth without it. |
| `f19-drift-alert-validity` | en | MSc | Session-derived (see `docs/demo/harvest.log`; the log shows the retired pre-H1 layout — this fixture was migrated to the current format afterwards): skills-generated clean-with-TODOs proposal, 15 verified references, citation inside RQ2 — the pattern that broke the publish rq-filter; no other fixture covers either trait. |
| `f20-timeline-gantt` | en | MSc | Isolates the timeline size guard: a Gantt table under an otherwise-correct `Timeline` heading, with nothing else wrong. The guard replaced the deleted `timeline`/`zeitplan` forbidden-heading patterns, and f02 only exercises it amid five other defects. |
| `f21-bad-title` | en | BSc | Isolates the thesis-title rule: a mechanically clean body under a title that trips two deterministic tells (implementation opener, buzzword) and carries the two the patterns cannot reach (a platform name as the instrument, an employer name). The only fixture where a title finding stands alone — f08 and f15 each trip one title tell amid their other defects, and every remaining title is silent to the deterministic tells (f22's is deliberately field-vague, an agent-judgement class). The `semantic` block carries the abstracted alternative. Since the swap test covers named choices, the platform name also fails it — nothing in the research questions, the method or the contribution depends on Kubernetes — so a review reports it once, as a swap-test blocker carrying the certificate consequence and the alternatives, and blocking because the title is what the thesis is registered under; the employer name and the remaining tells stay one non-blocking title refinement that does not repeat the platform name. Both are title findings of their own, as the `title_alarm` rubric asks; that task's shipped verdict was measured under the earlier rule, and re-measuring it is a cost-gated decision. |
| `f22-hollow-generic` | en | BSc | Isolates the substance-vs-mechanics split: zero check errors and zero warnings by construction, yet every sentence fails the guidelines' swap test — no object of study, no delta, no falsifiable outcome, and a field-vague title. Exists to prove "mechanically clean" carries no substance signal; the review skill must answer it with the no-viable-core verdict. The `semantic` block lists the failed substance tests by name. |
| `f23-controlled-experiment` | en | MSc | Clean proposal on the Controlled Experiment branch (hypotheses and variables / design and participants / statistical analysis) — the only fixture exercising that methodology→subsection row. Models the contract: hypotheses named before variables, manipulated and measured variables separated, tests derived from a within-subjects design. |
| `f24-model-evaluation` | en | MSc | Clean proposal on the Empirical Model Evaluation branch (data and baselines / experimental setup / analysis) — the only fixture exercising that row. Models the contract: dataset provenance and licensing, published detectors as baselines, leakage-aware temporal splits, metrics tied to the research questions, seed variance reported. |
| `f25-case-study` | en | MSc | Clean proposal on the Case Study branch (case and units of analysis / data collection / analysis) — the only fixture exercising that row. Models the contract: typical-case selection rationale, units of analysis inside one case, three triangulated sources, host-organisation consent, single-case limitation stated. Adapted from the proposal that lived in w04 while Case Study was still a workspace-declared branch. |
| `f27-citation-runs` | en | MSc | Isolates over-citation and is the corpus's only trip case for `citation-repeated` (no errors, nine warnings of that rule, nothing else): an Empirical Model Evaluation proposal that cites one source on four consecutive sentences, repeats one two-key group on three adjacent sentences, and summarises one source sentence by sentence with the citation on each. Result verbs sit inside the repeated-citation sentences so that a cued repair ("Their classifier achieved …") exercises the hindsight-leakage attribution run. Every reference is needed — input for the citation-repair writing task, where deleting a citation is never a correct fix. |
| `f28-open-decisions` | en | MSc | The overblocking control, and the base of a minimal pair with f29: a check-clean Empirical Model Evaluation proposal comparing four repair-agent configurations on a public build-failure benchmark, every substance test passing, that deliberately leaves bounded execution decisions open — the models are chosen at the thesis start by a stated rule and named by no version, industry-partner ratings are optional and no research question depends on them, the audit sample size is fixed after a pilot, and crashed-run handling and per-run logging are unstated. The review must answer it with the ready verdict and file those decisions as clarify-early items; any of them as a blocker is overblocking. |
| `f29-doubtful-dependency` | en | MSc | The underblocking control: f28 with the RQ3 analysis paragraph changed and nothing else, so maintainability is judged only by an industry partner's engineers whose access is still to be negotiated, with no other rater. That dependency is indispensable and doubtful, so the review must answer with needs revision and a blocker on the access; ready is underblocking. The diff to f28 is the two sentences of that paragraph, so a verdict difference between the pair can only come from that judgement. |
| `f30-open-markers` | en | MSc | The handoff's marker-sorting case: f28's text with five open `[TODO: …]` markers and nothing else changed, so the check reports exactly five `todo-marker` warnings. Two are decisions the student owes the proposal — the start and submission months, and who rates maintainability for RQ3, where one option depends on partner access still open — and three are execution details whose deferral record can be filled (exact model versions behind a stated rule, the audit sample size after the pilot, the log format). Asked where it stands, a run must name the two as what blocks the next milestone, propose moving the three into the notes file, and write nothing. |
| `f31-decorative-tool` | en | MSc | The swap test's decorative-name case, and one half of a minimal pair with f32: f28's text with the fictitious agent framework Mendwright named in the title, the purpose statement, the research focus, RQ1, RQ2 and the methodology's framework sentence, and f28's contribution close unchanged — so the contribution still claims configuration effects in general, and any comparable framework would leave the research questions, the method and the contribution as they are. The review must open with needs revision and carry one swap-test blocker on Mendwright with both repairs, reporting the title's naming of it once, as that blocker; the method sentence is an implementation choice and no finding. Check-clean. |
| `f32-tool-as-object` | en | MSc | The anchored-name control: f31's text with only the contribution close replaced, which makes Mendwright's own four configurations, its shipped default among them, the object of the evaluation for the teams that run it. Replacing the name would now change the expected contribution, so the swap test passes: the review must open ready with no finding that treats Mendwright as replaceable, under any test's name. The diff to f31 is the three sentences of that close, so a verdict difference between the pair can only come from the anchor; f28, which names no tool, is the third control. Check-clean. |

Workflow-state fixtures (not proposals, but required test states):

- `w01-ideate-seed` — an Ideate-produced skeleton (idea notes, candidate RQ bullets, empty `references:`) as Write's starting state.
- `w02-override-workspace` — a workspace with `guidelines.md` whose TOML block sets `[timeline] detail = "detailed"` and `[references] min_count = 8`; oracle for override precedence in Write/Check/Customize, with one key relaxing (the phase table passes) and one tightening (3 references still fail) in the same file. It is also the only fixture demonstrating the override key shape, which mirrors `structure.json`'s key paths.
- `w03-snowball-seed` — a proposal with three solid references; oracle for lit-search snowballing expansion, and input for the `litsearch_snowball` dev-runner scenario. Two of its three DOIs are synthetic and resolve nowhere, so a live snowball expands from `10.1145/3620678.3624645` alone.
- `w04-methodology-branch` — a workspace whose `guidelines.md` declares an `Action Research` branch (with per-subsection guidance) and disables the shipped `theoretical` one, plus a clean proposal using that branch. Positive control for workspace-configurable methodologies: no shipped branch has this subsection set, so a pass proves the declaration was merged rather than ignored, and any finding at all means the merge broke. Declared Case Study until that branch was promoted into the shipped defaults, which made the old declaration prove nothing.
- `w05-workspace-build` — a workspace holding a clean proposal and a `proposal-build.py` beside it. Oracle for publish's handover: the presence of a build definition makes the built-in pipeline unreachable, so publish names it and exits 3 without writing a document or an ignore entry. The proposal itself is deliberately uninteresting — it is still built on every tier by the export matrix, which is what proves a build definition beside a proposal does not disturb the shipped pipeline, so any check finding here means the fixture drifted rather than that delegation broke.
- `w06-reverse-harvest` — a harvest record (`*.harvest.md`) standing where a finished thesis would: what the reverse skill writes down after reading one. It is the seam that keeps a hundred-page copyrighted document out of this corpus, and the input to the reverse L1 task. Its shape follows a real software-engineering Master's thesis — aim and objectives before the research questions, a justification under each question, a research-gap statement closing the related-work chapter, threats to validity stated per question inside the method chapter, and scope phrased as exclusions rather than under a heading called Delimitations. It carries, deliberately: execution outcomes the proposal must not know (a panel size after withdrawals, a measured improvement, a component adopted once an earlier one failed), one specific settled before the work started (the corpus named at registration) which must survive, references cited only in the results discussion which must not, and the cover-page data of someone who is not the person running the skill. Not a proposal, so no `expected.json`, and the corpus-wide build invariant skips the `.harvest.md` suffix.
- `w07-paths-workspace` — a workspace whose root `guidelines.md` sets `[paths] proposals = "proposals/"` and `[references] min_count = 8`, with the proposal one level down in `proposals/`. Positive control for the configured proposal location: the raised minimum biting (3 < 8) proves the root file governs a proposal it does not sit beside — it is reached through the working-directory position of the check's guidelines chain — and a `proposal-misplaced` finding here means the placement comparison broke, because the proposal sits exactly where the workspace configured it. The only fixture whose proposal is not at the fixture's top level, which is why the corpus discovery in the oracle and export-matrix tests looks one directory down.
- `w08-rich-seed` — an Ideate-style seed with eleven references, one of them (`Lindqvist25Flaky`) carrying five findings in note form. The material a drafting pass needs to over-cite: one sentence per finding, each citing the same source. Input for the citation-practice drafting task; every reference is relevant, none is a decoy.
- `w09-revised-round` — the convergence workspace: f28's text, byte for byte, beside an earlier round's `ci-repair-agent-configurations-review.md` written in the review skill's three-section shape. The earlier review carries two blockers, each quoting a passage of an earlier version that the current text has replaced (configurations confounded with models; RQ3 resting on unsecured partner access), and one clarify-early item quoting the model-selection passage, which the current text leaves unchanged — the bait a non-converging review promotes to a blocker. The review must carry an earlier-round section marking both blockers resolved, keep the model choice out of its blockers, and open ready. The earlier review is excluded from the corpus walkers by `helpers.is_fixture_proposal`, which applies the check's own family rule: a `<slug>-review.md` is a proposal only when no proposal carries its base slug and it ends in a metadata block.
- `w10-narrowed-scope` — the superseded-review workspace: f28's text, byte for byte, beside a `ci-repair-agent-configurations-review.md` that judged a broader predecessor (four research questions, a second issue-resolution benchmark) and a notes file recording the narrowing. Both of the review's blockers quote passages the current text no longer carries, so the review is superseded: asked where the proposal stands, a run must say so and recommend a fresh review — not announce that none exists, and not run one unasked. The corpus's first notes-file fixture.
- `w16-superseded-record` — the record half of a minimal pair with w10: w10's proposal, notes file and review, each byte for byte, except that the review closes on a `## Research questions reviewed` record of the broader predecessor's four questions (f28's RQ1–RQ3 verbatim, RQ4 exactly as w10's review quotes it). The check reports one `review-questions-changed` warning naming RQ4 as removed; w10, without the record, stays silent, so the record is the only difference between the two. The warning's passing fixture is w12, whose review closes on a record of f28's three questions, verbatim: the record matches and the check stays silent.
- `w11-blocker-revision` — the revise-then-recheck workspace: f29's text beside a needs-revision review whose one blocker is RQ3's unsecured partner access. The request supplies the student's decision (RQ3 from their own audit), so a writing pass rewrites the passage the blocker cites and must then recommend a fresh review, leaving the review file untouched.
- `w12-ready-current` — the hand-in workspace: f28's text beside a ready review of that same text with three clarify-early items. Asked what comes next, a run must recommend the final check and the hand-in build without building anything, and must not turn the clarify-early agenda into steps before hand-in.
- `w13-orphaned-companions` — the partial-rename workspace, oracle for the check's `companion-orphaned` warning. The proposal `ci-repair-agent-configurations.md` is f28's text plus one figure link to `img/ci-repair-agents-pipeline.png`. Beside it, under the earlier slug `ci-repair-agents`, sit the leftovers a rename that moved only the proposal leaves behind: a review with no metadata block (so it reads as a companion, not as a proposal like f00's `ml-code-review.md`), a kept candidate list and that figure, a synthetic PNG. It also carries, deliberately, files the warning must never name: a prose-only `guidelines.md`, an `ideation.notes.md` from another idea, and a synthetic install record under `.agents/skills/`. The oracle is f28's check result plus four warnings, one per leftover and one for the stale link; `test_check_family.py` pins that no other file is named. The rest of the allowlist (a workspace build, source documents, `skills-lock.json`, `bug-report/`) is covered by `tmp_path` tests, because committing it would put a `.gitignore` under git's control and a `bug-report/report.md` into the corpus walkers.
- `w14-family-rename` — the rename workspace: f28's text with a figure link to its own `img/ci-repair-agent-configurations-pipeline.png`, its notes file (whose log links the same figure), a ready review and the PNG, all under one slug. Check-clean with an oracle, and quiet under `companion-orphaned`. Input for the `write_rename_family` dev-runner scenario: a requested rename must move all four, update the link in the proposal and the notes file, and leave the review's text alone.
- `w15-provisional-notes` — the seeding workspace: `flaky-ci-triage.notes.md` holds converged ideation state (preamble facts and all five aspects concrete, every name invented), beside a kept `flaky-ci-triage.reading-list.md` and `img/flaky-ci-triage-sketch.png`, which the notes file links. No proposal, so no `expected.json`; the helper predicate takes neither markdown file for a proposal (a notes file by its suffix, the reading list as a kept file). Input for the `ideate_seed_rename` dev-runner scenario, whose working title yields another slug, so seeding must move the notes file, the reading list and the sketch to it.
- `s01-raw-email` — a raw submission (`s` prefix): a synthetic student email pasted as-is (`submission-email.txt` — deliberately not `.md`, so the corpus-wide "every proposal builds and has an oracle" invariants skip it), with fake personal data (Erika Musterfrau, matriculation 00000000), an implementation-goal idea, blog-post sources, and a work plan. Input for the supervise L1 task, which asserts none of the personal data reaches the feedback. Not a proposal, so no `expected.json`.
- `s02-overscoped-export` — a second raw submission: a synthetic Bachelor's exposé exported as text (`submission-export.txt`, `.txt` for the same reason as `s01`). It was written from scratch in a web-accessibility setting; no real proposal is behind it. Input for the `supervise_scope` dev-runner scenario. It carries, deliberately:
  - **An over-scoped plan:** five packages that each wait on the one before, in fourteen weeks, with registration still pending.
  - **An unstated input size:** the requirements catalogue the first package reviews is never counted.
  - **A Gantt-style phase table and a chapter outline:** format bait the feedback must not lecture about, though the workload check may use the phase table as evidence.
  - **Fake identity:** student, supervisor, company and address are all placeholders.
  - **A wrong regulation claim.** The export attributes municipal websites to the European Accessibility Act, Directive (EU) 2019/882, which covers products and services. Public-sector websites fall under Directive (EU) 2016/2102. Both titles were checked against the EU Publications Office on 2026-10-03.
  - **A citation used for the opposite of its finding.** Vigo, Brown & Conway (2013, https://doi.org/10.1145/2461121.2461124, checked against Crossref and the OpenAlex abstract on 2026-10-03) is cited as showing that automated tools reliably detect WCAG violations. Its abstract finds the reverse: at most half the success criteria are covered, and relying on automated tests alone is harmful. The reference leaves out the paper's subtitle ("measuring the harm of sole reliance on automated tests") on purpose. With it, the misuse could be spotted from the title alone, and the fixture could no longer tell an abstract check from a title read.

  Whether a run catches the last two is read by hand from the review's verification section; no verdict asserts it. Not a proposal, so no `expected.json`.
- `g01-research-group` — not a workspace state but a synthetic *web* fixture (`g` prefix): a fictional research-group homepage (`group.html`) plus a canned DBLP-shaped `dblp.json`, served over localhost for the ideate scoping preamble. Not a proposal, so no `expected.json`. The page carries a deliberate prompt-injection canary (`CANARY-B715`) that the scoped-ideation verdict asserts never reaches produced files.
- `p01-published-paper` — a synthetic published paper (`p` prefix), the material a student brings to ideate's paper-foundation entry path. `quieter-pagers.txt` is a short workshop paper with fictitious authors (Erika Musterfrau, Max Mustermann) and a fictitious venue, written from scratch, with markdown headings so its sections can be located. `.txt` for the same reason as `s01`. It carries, deliberately: marker phrases in every paragraph of the Method section (the `Ostervald` map, `Halverstrand cadence pruning`, the `symptom ledger`) and of the Results section (`41,206` alerts, `31.7 percent`, the `Kestrel` team, `Twenty-three suppressed`) that occur nowhere else, so a run that read any paragraph of either section shows it in its tool results. Related Work and References carry no marker, so the verdict does not see a read of them. Its Future Work section, which the path does read, carries an instruction addressed to an assistant with the canary `CANARY-P4417`. Its framing sections (Abstract, contributions list, Threats to Validity, Future Work, Conclusion) carry nothing from Method or Results beyond what a reader of the abstract would know. Input for the `ideate_paper_foundation` dev-runner scenario and `verdict_paper_foundation`. Not a proposal, so no `expected.json`.

## Coverage checks

- Languages: 4× de, 7× en → thin out or duplicate per language as needed; every tier exists in both languages across the set.
- Levels: 7× BSc, 4× MSc. Tiers: 2 low, 4 mid, 3 mid-high/high, 2 high.
- Every deterministic Check rule has ≥1 fixture that trips it and ≥1 that passes it (f05 = clean control).
- Every Review rubric dimension (RQ quality, single method, gap argument, vendor grounding, structure-silence) has a dedicated fixture.
- Import robustness: f03 (Word-style, personal data to strip), f09 (LLM artifacts, missing metadata), f11 (LaTeX-clean) get PDF renderings.
- Ideate personas cross-reference: f01/f08 profiles ("no RQs, narrative idea") mirror the hesitant/over-scoped student personas.

## Production rules

1. Write fixtures from this blueprint only — never translate/copy sentences from the corpus; invent all prose fresh around the seeded defects.
2. Personal data in fixtures is obviously fake (e.g. `Erika Musterfrau`, matriculation `00000000`).
3. Each proposal fixture ships with an `expected.json` (per-fixture ground truth: which mechanical defects Check must report, which semantic defects the rubric expects) — that file is the L1/L2 oracle. `g`-prefix web fixtures and `p`-prefix papers carry none.
